content:
Like many of you, I've probably spent time on Wikipedia clicking around, randomly browsing different entries. Now there's finally an official app—but honestly, it's just a small tool that lets you do exactly that.

Now there's finally another button that can take you directly to a random Wikipedia article.

Today's update of the Wikipedia iOS app adds a fun and practical new feature: a "Random Article" widget that you can place on the home screen of your iPhone or iPad.

The widget comes in both large and medium sizes, and even has a cute mascot.

Tap the widget once and it will take you to a completely random Wikipedia article, opening it in random mode.

You don't need to exit the app and tap the widget again—just press the "Random" button and you can keep rolling the dice, diving deeper and deeper into this random maze.

Have fun, but be careful not to lose track of time. Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app also added a historical trivia mini-game.

After updating the Wikipedia app on your iPhone and iPad today, you can find this brand-new widget.

Enjoy your Apple device to the fullest!
